title: Manchuria Opium Squad
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: In 1937, Isamu Higata, a Japanese soldier in the puppet state of Manchukuo, loses the sight in one eye and is sent to an agricultural unit where officers abuse him. He finds poppies and begins producing high-grade opium to pay for his sick mother's care, which draws him into gangs, the army and the state's own drug trade (Kodansha blurb via AniList and MangaUpdates).
life_message: Survival and protecting one's family can push a decent person into crime in a corrupt, brutal place, at a mounting moral cost.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Disputes settled by guns, gangs and personal revenge in a lawless frontier (Kodansha page; MU Organized Crime).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Hero works outside every law, against army and state (blurb).

Civic vs kin.evidence: Saving his mother and family justifies everything (Kodansha blurb).

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Rank-based army abuse and gang bosses; hero resents but uses hierarchy.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Hero's botanical expertise and business logic drive the plot.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: 'The cheapest thing you'll find is a person's life' (Kodansha blurb via MU).

folkways.japan: Set in Japanese-occupied Manchukuo, it depicts the Japanese imperial army's rank abuse and the colonial opium economy, described as historical context.

delivery.evidence: Publisher copy frames it as a survival thriller; no source calls it preachy (to verify).
delivery.note: Moral weight is carried by the hero's escalating choices rather than stated lessons, per summaries.

winners_losers: Sympathy rests with Isamu and his family as underdogs; the army, gangs and the state are shown as predators, while the drug's victims bear the cost.
